data.why: The repository ships example CSVs used by its own tests that match the tidy factors+response format the Data Analysis and Bayesian Optimization pages expect from an uploaded file.

goals: Generate a Design of Experiment (DoE) for a new process with a given set of factors and levels, choosing between Sobol, full/fractional factorial, or definitive screening designs
Upload results from a completed set of experiments and get Bayesian-Optimization-suggested next experiments to try, optionally with multiple outcomes and constraints
Inspect model interpretation plots (e.g. Ax sensitivity analysis) to understand which factors drive the outcome
Upload experimental data and fit a linear regression or machine learning model (e.g. ElasticNetCV, Random Forest, Gradient Boosting) to analyze and visualize the response surface of a process
Download a generated design, suggested trials, or a plot (with underlying JSON data) to take back into the lab

review.summary: The tree states OPTIMEO's purpose and its three-stage structure (design → BO suggestions → analysis) accurately, the cited screens match their nodes, and labels are clean at the right granularity. It leaves out the ML-modelling, prediction and multi-objective/Pareto uses that the README and paper emphasise, includes failed-run steps as if they were workflow, and does not record a filter bug the replay found, so it needs fixes before filing.
